questions.question: What is the name of Chris's brother in "Everybody Hates Chris"?
In which British seaside town was the BBC sitcom "Fawlty Towers" set?
On the show "Rick and Morty", in episode "Total Rickall", who was a parasite?
In "The Big Bang Theory", what is Howard Wolowitz's nickname in World of Warcraft?
Who was the first Big Brother US winner to win with a perfect game?
Who was the winner of "Big Brother" Season 10?
Who created the animated TV show South Park?
questions.explanation: South Park was created by Trey Parker and Matt Stone and first aired on Comedy Central in 1997. The show follows four foul-mouthed boys in a fictional Colorado mountain town and is known for its sharp satirical humor. It remains one of the longest-running animated series in television history.

questions.question: What phrase is used to describe the moment when a TV series begins to decline in quality?
questions.explanation: The phrase "jump the shark" originated from a 1977 episode of Happy Days in which Fonzie literally jumps over a shark on water skis — widely seen as the moment the show lost its edge. It has since become a popular idiom for the turning point when any TV series (or other creative work) starts going downhill.

questions.question: Which actor on the sitcom Superstore also held the uncommon dual role of executive producer on the same show?
questions.explanation: Ben Feldman, known for his role as Jonah on Superstore, also served as an executive producer of the NBC series — a rare arrangement that put him both in front of and behind the camera. This kind of dual on-screen/producing credit is more commonly seen with veteran stars who have significant leverage in a show's production. Superstore ran for six seasons from 2015 to 2021.

questions.question: Which co-creator of the R-rated Hulu "traumedy" set in the year 2000 coined that term to describe the show's middle-school setting?
questions.explanation: Anna Konkle, who co-created and stars in PEN15 alongside Maya Erskine, described the show as a "traumedy" — a blend of trauma and comedy — to capture its unflinching, R-rated look at middle school life set in the year 2000. The series is notable for Konkle and Erskine playing 13-year-old versions of themselves as adults alongside actual child actors. PEN15 aired on Hulu from 2019 to 2021.
